question.text: A body is at rest at $x=0$. At $t=0$, it starts moving in the positive $x$-direction with a constant acceleration. At the same instant another body passes through $x=0$ moving in the positive $x$ direction with a constant speed. The position of the first body is given by $\mathrm{x}_1(\mathrm{t})$ after time ' $\mathrm{t}$ ' and that of the second body by $x_2(t)$ after the same time interval. Which of the following graphs correctly describes $\left(x_1-x_2\right)$ as a function of time ' $t$ '?

solution.text:
$$
\begin{aligned}
& x_1(t)=\frac{1}{2} a t^2 \\
& x_2(t)=v t \\
& x_1-x_2=\frac{1}{2} a t^2-v t
\end{aligned}
$$
